question: Should package-owner/security review accept opt-in local packaged `dist` override replay plus strict content-inventory enforcement as the package-update contract?
rationale: The implementation appears defensively structured, but it intentionally changes update compatibility and local filesystem mutation behavior, which needs owner acceptance beyond automated correctness review.

options.title: Accept After Owner Review
options.body: Land the branch once the assigned package/update owner accepts the compatibility and security-boundary posture.

options.title: Narrow To Preserve-Only
options.body: Remove or defer `--reapply-local-overrides` if maintainers want recovery bundles without automatic replay mutation risk.

options.title: Keep Draft Paused
options.body: Leave the branch open until package/update ownership decides whether local package override replay is a supported scenario.

recommendation.title: Accept After Owner Review
recommendation.body: Land the branch once the assigned package/update owner accepts the compatibility and security-boundary posture.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the PR and introduced the core updater surface this PR extends.
